nodes.name: Pure Ni spray-coating
nodes.procedure: Nickel Mesh (NM) substrate was coated with pure nickel precursor solution using a high-temperature spray-coating method to form Ni/NM electrode with surface catalytic layer.
nodes.source_text: A series of NiCe/NM (Nickel Mesh) electrodes with different Ce content in the surface catalytic layer were synthesized... compared to the pure Ni electrode (Ni/NM)

nodes.name: NiCe spray-coating (various ratios)
nodes.procedure: Nickel Mesh (NM) substrate was coated with nickel-cerium precursor mixture solution with different Ce to Ni ratios (0.2, 15, and 3000 ppm for L, M, and H respectively) using a high-temperature spray-coating method to form NiCe_L/NM, NiCe_M/NM, and NiCe_H/NM electrodes with surface catalytic layer containing highly dispersed or aggregated cerium.
nodes.source_text: A series of NiCe/NM (Nickel Mesh) electrodes with different Ce content in the surface catalytic layer were synthesized and evaluated... Three of them with Ce to Ni ratios of 0.2, 15, and 3000 ppm, denoted as L, M, and H

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows similar rough morphology for Ni/NM and NiCe_M/NM catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) shows the relatively smooth surface of the NM substrate and a similar rough morphology of Ni/NM and NiCe_M / NM (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM of NiCe_M/NM shows interplanar spacings of 0.203 nm (Ni 111) and 0.176 nm (Ni 200), 0.241 nm (NiO 111), and discrete bright dots assigned to highly dispersed cerium.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a displays the crystalline structure of NiCe_M / NM , analyzed by aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (TEM) in a high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) model. Evidence from interplanar spacings of 0.203 and 0.176 nm , corresponding to the (1 1 1) and (2 0 0) planes of Ni...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM of NiCe_H/NM shows large bright region up to 3.80 nm with interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm indicating cerium aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, a large bright region with a size of up to 3.80 nm can be found in the HAADF images of NiCe_H / NM in Figure 2d.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ce 3d spectrum of NiCe_M/NM shows binding energy range 885-920 eV confirming Ce existence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c confirms the existence of Ce from the XPS spectrum with a binding energy of 885 - 920 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines Ce:Ni atomic ratio for NiCe_M/NM at ppm level, NiCe_L/NM two orders smaller, NiCe_H/NM about 1/1000 Ni in particle form.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific ratio of Ce to Ni in the matrix is determined by inductive coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) (Table S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows reduced impedance for NiCe_M/NM (≈5 Ω cm² at 125 mV) compared to Ni/NM (≈12 Ω cm²), smaller R_ct, and higher double layer capacitance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots in Figure 4d,e give the impedance of Ni/NM and NiCe_M / NM at different overpotentials, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPD shows primary H2 desorption on NiCe_M/NM begins at lower temperature with significantly higher desorbed H2 quantity than Ni/NM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, temperature-programmed desorption of H2 ( H2 -TPD) (Figure S9, Supporting Information) reveals that the primary desorption of H2 on NiCe_M / NM begins at a lower temperature...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD consistent with TEM showing Ni as main component of NiCe_M/NM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: confirms that the main component of the NiCe_M / NM electrode is Ni, consistent with the XRD result (Figure S3, Supporting Information).
